title: Optimal and Near-Optimal Constructions for Bootstrap Percolation in Hypercubes
summary: The $r$-neighbour bootstrap process on a graph $G$ begins with a set of infected vertices; subsequently, healthy vertices become infected once they have at least $r$ infected neighbours. The central extremal problem in bootstrap percolation is to determine the minimum cardinality of an initial infected set that eventually spreads to all vertices of $G$, denoted $m(G;r)$. Morrison and Noel established a general lower bound on $m(Q_d;r)$, where $Q_d$ is the $d$-dimensional hypercube, and asked whether it is tight whenever $d$ is sufficiently large with respect to $r$.
